newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Dec extends gains late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Dec extends gains late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed and the December contract closed at a two-month high, extending gains late after hitting buy stops toward the close, traders said.
Traders said Cargill was a key player, covering its short positions by buying KCBT Dec and selling KCBT March.

"It started off weaker because of the poor close we saw last night, but buying came in outright in the December while Cargill continued to be a seller of March," a KCBT trader said. "Then on the close we saw... buying after some small buy stops were hit."
Traders said the December/March inversion widened again as a result of short covering. The spread traded late at 43 cents, up from its close Thursday at 39 cents.

KCBT wheat closed five cents per bushel lower to 7-1/2 cents higher, with Dec up 7-1/2 cents at $4.47-1/2 a bushel. The last time Dec closed higher was on Sept. 10, when it closed at $4.52 per bushel.

Cargill bought at least one million December bushels and one million March but also sold 2.6 million March. Prudential bought 1.2 million Dec, sold one million March and bear-spread one million March/Dec at 38 to 40 cents.
Prudential also bull-spread two million March/July at 28 to 30 cents.
"Cargill is perceived short (wheat) at the Gulf, so it would make sense that they'd be bidding for Dec wheat," a trader said.
